claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-2:DonHang.Api/Program.cs:32 `builder.Services.AddHostedService<NotificationSender>();`. Docs: "The hosted service is activated once at app startup and gracefully shut down at app shutdown." Each api process has its own host, so each runs one NotificationSender against the shared database.

"Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL." "a SELECT query (without a FOR UPDATE/SHARE clause) sees only data committed before the query began; it never sees either uncommitted data or changes committed by concurrent transactions during the query's execution."

"FOR UPDATE causes the rows retrieved by the SELECT statement to be locked as though for update. This prevents them from being locked, modified or deleted by other transactions until the current transaction ends. That is, other transactions that attempt UPDATE, DELETE, SELECT FOR UPDATE, ... of these rows will be blocked until the current transaction ends". Live: a FOR UPDATE NOWAIT on a row held by another open transaction failed with "could not obtain lock on row in relation \"notifications\"".
claim_verdicts.source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html, 13.3.2 Row-Level Locks (WebFetch); live psql in donhang-db, 2026-09-28

claim_verdicts.evidence: "With SKIP LOCKED, any selected rows that cannot be immediately locked are skipped. Skipping locked rows provides an inconsistent view of the data, so this is not suitable for general purpose work, but can be used to avoid lock contention with multiple consumers accessing a queue-like table."

"Row-level locks do not affect data querying; they block only writers and lockers to the same row." "Row-level locks are released at transaction end or during savepoint rollback". Live: plain SELECT of a row locked FOR UPDATE by an idle-in-transaction session returned `44|pending` at once; skip-locked.sh session D printed all four demo rows while A held two.

"For either normal or abnormal termination, any open transaction is rolled back, not committed." Live: a psql holding FOR UPDATE on a demo row (state 'idle in transaction') was killed; its backend disappeared from pg_stat_activity and a new FOR UPDATE NOWAIT on the row returned it at once.

claim_verdicts.evidence: lock_timeout: "Abort any statement that waits longer than the specified amount of time while attempting to acquire a lock on a table, index, row, or other database object. ... The limit applies both to explicit locking requests (such as LOCK TABLE, or SELECT FOR UPDATE without NOWAIT) ..." Live: session C printed "ERROR:  canceling statement due to lock timeout".

"To prevent the operation from waiting for other transactions to commit, use either the NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED option." i.e. without them a locking SELECT waits. Live: session C (FOR UPDATE without SKIP LOCKED) waited until lock_timeout cancelled it.

Follows from the code rather than preference: the transaction opened in ClaimDueAsync stays open across every SendOneAsync of the batch until CompleteAsync commits (NotificationSender.cs:53-58), and row locks last until transaction end (13.3.2). Fewer rows per claim means fewer sends inside the transaction.
